title: 把: doing something to something
explain: 把 puts the object in front of the verb, so you can say what you do to it and what becomes of it: 我把门关上了 'I closed the door'. The pattern is Subject + 把 + object + verb + something extra (a result, a place, or 了).
The verb cannot stand alone after 把. Add a result, a place, a direction or 了: 请把门打开 'Please open the door'; 请把书放在桌子上 'Please put the book on the table'; 我把作业做完了 'I have finished my homework'.
The object after 把 should be something known (the, this, that), not 'a' something. Say 把这本书给我 'Give me this book', not 把一本书给我.
A negative goes before 把: 我没把作业做完 'I did not finish the homework'; 别把手机丢了 'Don't lose your phone'.

examples.en: Please open the door.
I have finished my homework.
Please put the book on the table.
He has broken the cup.

mistakes: Do not use 把 with a bare verb: 我把书看 is wrong. Add a result or 了: 我把书看完了 'I have finished the book'.
The negative goes before 把, not before the verb: 我没把作业做完, not 我把作业没做完.

q.en: He has closed the door.
q.explain: Subject + 把 + object + verb + result + 了.

q.en: Please give me the phone.
q.explain: 把 + object comes before the verb 给.

q.en: I have put the book on the table.
q.explain: 把 brings the object in front of the verb.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Please close the door?
q.en: Please close the door.
q.explain: The object comes right after 把, before the verb.

q.en: I did not finish the homework.

title: 被: something is done to it
explain: 被 turns the sentence around. Instead of 'he broke the cup' (他打坏了杯子) you can say what happened to the cup: 杯子被他打坏了 'The cup was broken by him'.
The pattern is Thing + 被 + (doer) + verb + result or 了. Like 把, the verb needs something extra. The doer can be left out: 我的书被借走了 'My book has been borrowed'.
被 is most often used when something unwanted or unexpected happens to the thing: 我的伞被朋友拿走了 'My umbrella was taken away by a friend'. In speech 让 and 叫 can replace 被: 杯子让他打坏了.
A negative goes before 被: 我的书没被借走 'My book was not borrowed'.

examples.en: The cup was broken by him.
My umbrella was taken away by a friend.
The homework was collected by the teacher.
My book was borrowed by a classmate.

mistakes: Do not use a bare verb after 被: 杯子被他打 is incomplete. Say 杯子被他打坏了.
The negative goes before 被: 我的书没被借走, not 我的书被没借走.

q.en: The cup was broken by him.
q.explain: Thing + 被 + doer + verb + result + 了.

q.en: My book was borrowed.
q.explain: The doer can be left out.

q.en: My umbrella was taken away by a friend.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: The homework was collected by the teacher?
q.en: The homework was collected by the teacher.
My book was not borrowed.

title: 如果…就… and 的话: if
explain: 如果 means 'if'. The condition comes first and the result second, and the result usually has 就 (or 会) before its verb: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了 'If it rains tomorrow, we won't go'.
的话 can close the condition, with or without 如果: 你累的话，就休息一下 'If you are tired, take a rest'. Using both is fine: 如果你累的话，就休息一下.
Do not put 就 in the condition part. It belongs to the result: 如果天气好，我们就去爬山 'If the weather is good, we will go climbing'.
你想去的话，就跟我们一起去 'If you want to go, then come with us' shows that 就 can also mean 'in that case'.

examples.zh: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了。
examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
If you are tired, take a rest.
If you have no money, you cannot buy it.

examples.zh: 如果天气好，我们就去爬山。
examples.en: If the weather is good, we will go climbing.

mistakes: Put the condition first: 如果明天下雨，我们不去. Do not start with the result.
Do not put 就 in the condition: 如果你就有时间 is wrong. 就 goes in the result part.

q.en: If it rains, we won't go.
If you are tired, then rest.
If you have money, then buy it.

q.zh: 明天下雨的话，我们就不去了。
q.en: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: If I have time, I will go?
q.en: If I have time, I will go.
q.explain: The 如果 part comes first.

title: 不但…而且…, 而且, 可是 and 然后
explain: 不但…而且… means 'not only … but also …': 这个菜不但便宜，而且好吃 'This dish is not only cheap but also delicious'. When both parts have the same subject, put 不但 after the subject: 她不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞.
而且 alone means 'moreover, and also': 今天很冷，而且下雨了 'It is cold today, and it has started raining'.
可是 means 'but': 这个很好看，可是有点儿贵 'This looks nice, but it is a bit expensive'. It is a little more spoken than 但是.
然后 means 'then, after that': 我们先看电影，然后去吃饭 'We will watch a movie first, and then go and eat'.

examples.zh: 这个饭馆不但很便宜，而且很好吃。
examples.en: This restaurant is not only cheap but also delicious.
It is cold today, and it has started raining.

examples.zh: 这个很好看，可是有点儿贵。
examples.en: This looks nice, but it is a bit expensive.

examples.zh: 我们先看电影，然后去吃饭。
examples.en: We will watch a movie first, and then go and eat.

mistakes: Use 不但 with 而且, not with 但是 or 可是: 不但…而且… go together.
而且 comes at the start of the second part: do not put it before the first part.

q.zh: 这个菜不但便宜，而且好吃。
q.en: This dish is not only cheap but also delicious.
q.explain: 不但 + first part, 而且 + second part.

q.en: I want to go, but I have no time.
q.explain: 可是 starts the part that goes against the first.

q.zh: 他不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞。
q.en: He can not only sing but also dance.
q.explain: The second part starts with 而且.

q.en: Eat first, then watch a movie.
q.explain: 然后 means then, after that.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: This looks nice, but it is expensive?
q.en: This looks nice, but it is expensive.

title: 只要…就… and 只有…才…
explain: 只要…就… means 'as long as … then …': 只要天气好，我们就去公园 'As long as the weather is good, we go to the park'. The condition is easy to meet, and the result follows.
只有…才… means 'only if … then …': 只有多练习，才能说好汉语 'Only by practising more can you speak Chinese well'. The condition is the one and only way.
Compare: 只要你来，我就去 'As long as you come, I will go' (that is enough) and 只有你来，我才去 'I will go only if you come' (nobody else will do).
才 here means 'only then', and it goes before the verb of the result.

examples.zh: 只要天气好，我们就去公园。
examples.en: As long as the weather is good, we go to the park.
As long as you listen more, you will understand.
Only by speaking more can you speak well.
I will go only if you come.

mistakes: Do not mix the pairs: 只要 goes with 就 and 只有 goes with 才. 只要…才… is wrong.
The result part keeps its verb after 就 or 才: 只有你来，我才去, not 只有你来，才我去.

q.en: As long as you work hard, you can learn it well.

q.zh: 只有你多练习，才能说好。
q.en: Only if you practise more can you speak well.
As long as the weather is good, we will go.
I will go only if you come.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Only with practice can one improve?
q.en: Only with practice can one improve.

title: 除了…, 都 / 还…: except and besides
explain: 除了 A，都… means 'except A, everyone or everything …': 除了星期天，我每天都上班 'Except for Sunday, I go to work every day'; 除了他，大家都来了 'Everyone came except him'.
除了 A，还 / 也… means 'besides A, also …': 除了苹果，我还买了西瓜 'Apart from apples, I also bought watermelon'.
以外 is optional and goes after A: 除了他以外，大家都来了. It does not change the meaning.
The ending shows which meaning you want: 都 for 'all the rest', 还 or 也 for 'in addition'.

examples.zh: 除了周末，我每天都学汉语。
examples.en: Except for weekends, I study Chinese every day.
Besides rice, I also want to eat fish.

examples.zh: 除了你以外，我谁都不认识。
examples.en: Except for you, I do not know anyone.

examples.zh: 除了哥哥，大家都喜欢运动。
examples.en: Except for my older brother, everyone likes sports.

mistakes: 除了 alone is not a full sentence. Finish it with 都 ('all the rest') or 还 / 也 ('in addition').
Do not mix the two meanings: 除了…都… takes something away, 除了…还… adds something.

q.en: Everyone came except him.
q.explain: 除了 + A, 大家都 + verb.

q.en: Besides rice, I also want fish.

q.zh: 除了星期天，我每天都学习。
q.en: Except for Sunday, I study every day.

q.zh: 除了苹果，我还喜欢西瓜。
q.en: Besides apples, I also like watermelon.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Everyone is here except Mom?
q.en: Everyone is here except Mom.

title: 为了, 为, 关于 and 根据
explain: 为了 + goal means 'in order to, for the sake of': 为了学好汉语，他每天都练习 'In order to learn Chinese well, he practises every day'. The goal comes first, then what you do.
为 + person + verb means 'for someone': 妈妈为孩子准备了早饭 'Mom prepared breakfast for the child'. 我为你高兴 means 'I am happy for you'.
关于 + topic means 'about': 我想看一个关于中国的电影 'I want to watch a movie about China'. 关于这件事，我不知道 'About this matter, I do not know'.
根据 means 'according to, based on': 根据地图，银行在前面 'According to the map, the bank is ahead'.

examples.zh: 为了去中国学习，他在学汉语。
examples.en: In order to study in China, he is learning Chinese.

examples.zh: 妈妈为孩子准备了早饭。
examples.en: Mom prepared breakfast for the child.

examples.zh: 我想看一个关于中国的电影。
examples.en: I want to watch a movie about China.

examples.zh: 根据他的话，火车晚点了。
examples.en: According to what he says, the train is late.

mistakes: 为了 gives a goal, 因为 gives a reason. Say 为了考试，他每天学习 'He studies every day to prepare for the exam', not 因为考试 when you mean a goal.
关于 needs a topic after it: 关于中国的书 is a book about China.

q.en: In order to study Chinese, he goes to China.
q.explain: 为了 + goal, then the action.

q.en: I want to read a book about China.
He cooked for us.
According to the map, the bank is ahead.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: This is a book about Chinese?
options: 这是一本关于汉语的书。
这是一本为了汉语的书。
q.zh: 这是一本关于汉语的书。
q.en: This is a book about Chinese.

title: 或者 and 还是: two kinds of "or"
explain: 或者 means 'or' in a statement: 我想喝茶或者咖啡 'I want tea or coffee'; 周末我想看电影或者去公园 'At the weekend I want to watch a movie or go to the park'. It says either one is fine.
还是 means 'or' in a question where you ask the other person to choose: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？ 'Do you want tea or coffee?'
In writing you may also see 或 on its own: 星期六或星期天.
So: statement → 或者, choice question → 还是.

examples.zh: 周末我想看电影或者去公园。
examples.en: At the weekend I want to watch a movie or go to the park.

examples.zh: 明天或者后天，我都有时间。
examples.en: Either tomorrow or the day after tomorrow, I have time.
Do you want tea or coffee?

examples.zh: 我们坐火车或者坐飞机去。
examples.en: We will go by train or by plane.

mistakes: Do not use 或者 in a question that asks someone to choose: say 你想喝茶还是咖啡？, not 你想喝茶或者咖啡？
Do not use 还是 for 'or' in a plain statement of choices: say 我想喝茶或者咖啡, not 我想喝茶还是咖啡.

q.en: I want tea or coffee.
q.explain: 或者 joins two choices in a statement.

q.en: Do you want tea or coffee?
q.explain: 还是 joins two choices in a question.

q.zh: 明天或者后天我有时间。
q.en: I have time tomorrow or the day after tomorrow.

q.zh: 你想坐火车还是坐飞机？
q.en: Do you want to go by train or by plane?

q.prompt: Which sentence is a correct statement?
q.en: I want tea or coffee.

title: 先…再…, 一边…一边… and 又…又…
explain: 先…再… means 'first … then …': 先洗手，再吃饭 'Wash your hands first, then eat'. 然后 can replace 再: 我们先看电影，然后去吃饭.
一边…一边… means 'while … (at the same time)': 妈妈一边做饭，一边听音乐 'Mom listens to music while she cooks'. 一边 goes before both verbs.
又…又… means 'both … and …' and joins two qualities: 这个菜又好吃又便宜 'This dish is both delicious and cheap'; 她又高又漂亮 'She is both tall and pretty'.

examples.en: Wash your hands first, then eat.

examples.zh: 妈妈一边做饭，一边听音乐。
examples.en: Mom cooks while listening to music.
This dish is both delicious and cheap.
I will go to the bank first, then to the shop.

mistakes: Put 一边 before both verbs: 他一边吃饭一边看电视. Do not leave out the first 一边.
又…又… joins two things of the same kind (two adjectives or two verbs): 又高又漂亮.

q.en: Wash your hands first, then eat.

q.zh: 他一边吃饭，一边看电视。
q.en: He watches TV while he eats.
q.explain: 一边 comes before both verbs.

q.en: Eat first, then watch a movie.
I will take a shower first, then go to bed.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: She is both tall and pretty?
q.en: She is both tall and pretty.

title: 又 and 再: two kinds of "again"
explain: Both 又 and 再 mean 'again', but 又 is for something that has already happened again, and 再 is for something that will happen again.
又 looks back: 他昨天迟到，今天又迟到了 'He was late yesterday, and again today'. The sentence usually ends with 了.
再 looks ahead: 请再说一遍 'Please say it once more'; 明天我再来 'I will come again tomorrow'.
A quick test: if you can say it with 'again, as it happened', use 又. If it is a request or a plan, use 再.

examples.en: He was late again today.
Please say it once more.

examples.zh: 我昨天去了，今天又去了。
examples.en: I went yesterday, and I went again today.
I will come again tomorrow.

mistakes: Do not use 再 for something that already happened: say 今天又来了, not 今天再来了.
Do not use 又 for a plan or a request: say 明天我再来, not 明天我又来.

q.en: He was late again today.
q.explain: 又 goes before the verb, 了 at the end.

q.en: Please say it once more.
q.explain: 再 goes before the verb in a request.

q.en: I will come again tomorrow.
It rained again today.
q.explain: 又 is for something that already happened again.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He came again (it already happened)?
q.en: He came again.
q.explain: 又 is for what has already happened.
